Provenance
Made by hand at a printmaking workshop, Namibia — September 2019

A relief print made by hand during a trip to the red sand dunes of Sossusvlei in the Namib-Naukluft National Park. The image captures the dune landscape from above — scattered desert plants in white against a deep burgundy-black ground, a smoldering horizon, the feeling of being very small inside something very large.

Namibia’s printmaking tradition has deep roots, shaped in part by the German colonial presence in cities like Swakopmund and a strong contemporary arts infrastructure that grew up around independence in 1990. Workshops where visitors make prints by hand continue that tradition.

This trip included sleeping under open stars in the red sand dunes — the kind of night that changes how you understand silence and scale.

The only print that exists. Edition 1/1.
